nodes.languageNotes: Deep-freezes the recipe catalog with Object.freeze at module load so consumers cannot mutate the shared bilingual data; scoring uses a weighted signal-phrase match rather than a full NLP model.

nodes.name: detectGuideLanguage
nodes.summary: Detects whether a query string is Chinese or English by testing for CJK Unicode code points.

nodes.name: localized
nodes.summary: Projects a raw bilingual recipe record into a single-language view (en or zh), shallow-copying its presentation settings and include list.

nodes.name: listScenarioRecipes
nodes.summary: Returns all scenario recipes localized to the requested language, defaulting to English.

nodes.name: scoreRecipe
nodes.summary: Scores how well a single recipe matches a free-text query by summing weighted signal-phrase matches, with an exact-id match short-circuiting to a perfect score.

nodes.name: recommendScenario
nodes.summary: Ranks all recipes against a user query, selects the highest-scoring recipe (or a safe default when nothing matches), and returns a localized recommendation with a confidence tier and up to two alternative suggestions.

nodes.name: formatScenarioList
nodes.summary: Renders the full catalog of scenario recipes as a human-readable, localized text listing for CLI display.

nodes.name: formatScenarioRecommendation
nodes.summary: Formats a recommendation result into a labeled, localized text block including use/avoid guidance, the copy-ready prompt, and any alternative fits, for CLI output.

nodes.name: publicGuideData
nodes.summary: Exports the full recipe catalog with both language variants and raw signal weights for external tooling such as docs generation.

nodes.name: makeFakeOpeners

nodes.name: extractSvgs
nodes.summary: Walks a parsed HTML/fragment document tree to collect top-level `<svg>` markup and recursively extracts SVGs embedded in iframe `srcdoc` attributes, returning separate direct and embedded document lists.

nodes.name: diagnostics.py
nodes.summary: Canonical diagnostics and result-serialization utilities: builds the normative tool envelope from findings and results, produces deterministic sorted JSON output, maps status strings to process exit codes, and computes reproducible sha256 digests over a set of source files.

nodes.name: create_parser
nodes.summary: Builds the top-level argparse parser for the `concorde` command, registering the validate, docsite, build, and protocol-manifest subcommands with their respective options.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Routes a parsed CLI invocation to the docsite, build, or validate implementation based on the selected subcommand, translating outcomes and caught errors into ToolResult/Finding objects.

nodes.name: _protocol_manifest

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses arguments, enforces the isolated-worktree guard for mutating subcommands, dispatches the tool, and always writes a canonical JSON envelope with the corresponding process exit code, even on unexpected exceptions.

nodes.name: finding_key
nodes.summary: Produces a deterministic sort key for a Finding from its rule ID, source, position, and message so findings can be ordered reproducibly in output.

nodes.name: finding_dict
nodes.summary: Converts a Finding dataclass instance into a plain dict, dropping None-valued fields to keep serialized JSON compact.

nodes.name: envelope
nodes.summary: Assembles the normative tool result envelope dict (schema_version, tool, target, status, artifacts, findings, result), sorting and deduplicating artifacts and findings for deterministic output.

nodes.name: tool_envelope
nodes.summary: Adapts a ToolResult object into the canonical envelope dict by delegating to envelope() with the ToolResult's fields.

nodes.name: canonical_json
nodes.summary: Serializes a value to deterministic, sorted, compact JSON text with a trailing newline, ensuring reproducible CLI output across runs.

nodes.name: exit_code
nodes.summary: Maps a tool result status string (success, invalid, conflict, failed, ...) to its corresponding process exit code, defaulting to 3 for unrecognized statuses.

nodes.name: digest_sources
nodes.summary: Computes a reproducible sha256 digest over a set of source files by hashing each relative path and its newline-normalized contents in sorted order.

nodes.name: lifecycle/README.md

nodes.name: sequence/README.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the sequence renderer: invocation, required JSON fields (participants/segments/messages/activations/cards), viewBox-driven timeline scaling, and schema location for diagram_type "sequence" documents.

nodes.name: workflow/README.md

nodes.name: generate-brand-marks.mjs

nodes.name: usage

nodes.name: extractRepoRootArgs
nodes.summary: Parses --repo-root/--repo-root=<path> out of a CLI argument list, resolving it to an absolute path and returning the remaining args.

nodes.name: diagnostic
nodes.summary: Builds a normalized diagnostic object (severity/code/message/subject/evidence/supportedFixes) used throughout the CLI's structured failure reporting.

nodes.name: inputDiagnostic
nodes.summary: Wraps a caught input-reading error (missing file, invalid JSON) into a classified diagnostic naming the offending input path.

nodes.name: rendererFailure
nodes.summary: Converts a failed spawnSync result from a renderer subprocess into diagnostics, parsing structured JSON stderr when present and falling back to a generic renderer-failure diagnostic.

nodes.name: checkerDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Translates artifact-checker composition issues and failed checks into classified diagnostics with code-specific supported fixes, guaranteeing at least one diagnostic on failure.

nodes.name: formatDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Formats an error message plus a list of diagnostics (with any supported fixes) into a single human-readable multi-line string.

nodes.name: reportCompareFailure
nodes.summary: Builds and prints (JSON or human-readable) a failed compare-command receipt with a single classified diagnostic, then sets the process exit code.

nodes.name: extractCompareOptions
nodes.summary: Parses the compare subcommand's options (--json, --receipt/--receipt=<path>) out of its argument list, failing on unknown flags.

nodes.name: commitComparePair
nodes.summary: Atomically commits a validated compare HTML candidate and its receipt from a staging directory to their final output paths, raising classified compareCommitError instances on failure.

nodes.name: renderValidatedArchitecture
nodes.summary: Runs the architecture renderer for a given input/output/quality/repoRoot combination and reports renderer failures as diagnostics.

nodes.name: commandCompare
nodes.summary: Implements `archify compare architecture <base> <head>`: renders both sides, builds the canonical architecture-delta receipt and annotated side-by-side HTML via architecture-delta.mjs, validates it, and commits the artifact plus receipt.

nodes.name: commandRender
nodes.summary: Implements `archify render <type> <input> [output]`: resolves the renderer path for the type and spawns it, exiting with the renderer's status.

nodes.name: reportDeliveryFailure
nodes.summary: Builds and prints a failed delivery receipt (JSON or human-readable) with its diagnostics and sets the process exit code.

nodes.name: reportValidateFailure
nodes.summary: Builds and prints a failed validate receipt (JSON or human-readable) with its diagnostics and sets the process exit code.

nodes.name: sourceEvidenceFromArtifact
nodes.summary: Extracts the repository source-evidence block recorded in a rendered artifact for inclusion in the delivery receipt.

nodes.name: commandDeliver
nodes.summary: Implements `archify deliver <type> <input> [output]`: the final-acceptance command that freezes the spec into a snapshot, renders and checks it, atomically commits the HTML, records SHA-256/byte-count receipts, and optionally opens the result.

nodes.name: commandPreview
nodes.summary: Implements `archify preview <type> <input> [output]`: renders a non-final HTML for an active authoring loop and optionally opens it locally.

nodes.name: commandVisualCheck

nodes.name: commandDoctor

nodes.name: commandGuide
nodes.summary: Implements `archify guide [scenario]`: helps an agent pick the correct diagram type for an ambiguous request, optionally in a specific language and JSON format.

nodes.name: commandBrands

nodes.name: commandDemo
nodes.summary: Implements `archify demo [output-directory]`: renders bundled example diagrams into a target directory as a quick end-to-end smoke check.

nodes.name: commandValidate
nodes.summary: Implements `archify validate <type> <input>`: runs schema and composition validation for a candidate diagram and reports pass/fail diagnostics (including the showcase 9-check acceptance bar) without producing final output.

nodes.name: ArchitectureDeltaError
nodes.summary: Custom Error subclass carrying a structured code/message/details payload used to fail closed on malformed or incomparable architecture-delta inputs.

nodes.name: canonicalArchitecture
nodes.summary: Produces a canonical, order-independent representation of an architecture diagram (repository, components, boundaries) so formatting and ordering differences never register as changes.

nodes.name: canonicalArchitectureJson
nodes.summary: Serializes canonicalArchitecture's output to stable, pretty-printed JSON for hashing or byte comparison.

nodes.name: stableIndex
nodes.summary: Indexes a list of architecture entities by stable ID, raising ArchitectureDeltaError on duplicate or missing IDs so downstream comparison never guesses identity.

nodes.name: boundaryIndex
nodes.summary: Indexes architecture boundaries by their computed key on a given side (base/head) for use in the comparison pipeline.

nodes.name: fieldChanges
nodes.summary: Computes per-field before/after change records for one entity by comparing normalized field groups between the two sides.

nodes.name: compareEntities
nodes.summary: Compares indexed base/head entities of a given kind (component, relationship, boundary) and classifies each as added, removed, or changed with per-field change groups.

nodes.name: presentationChanged
nodes.summary: Determines whether two architecture documents differ only in presentation (legend/visual settings) rather than topology, so legend-only edits are never reported as authored or geometry changes.

nodes.name: compareArchitecture
nodes.summary: Top-level comparison entry point: validates both sides' shape, canonicalizes them, classifies component/relationship/boundary changes and presentation drift, and returns the full compare receipt consumed by the CLI and the delta HTML builder.

nodes.name: extractArchitectureSvg
nodes.summary: Extracts the inline `<svg>` markup block from a rendered architecture HTML artifact.

nodes.name: extractArtifactCss
nodes.summary: Extracts the inline `<style>` CSS block from a rendered architecture HTML artifact for reuse inside the delta view.

nodes.name: addState
nodes.summary: Adds an added/removed/changed state marker to a change map for a tagged entity, allowing a forced state override.

nodes.name: nodeGroupRanges
nodes.summary: Scans raw SVG markup for component node `<g>` group boundaries, returning their character ranges for later transformation.

nodes.name: transformNodeGroups
nodes.summary: Applies a transform callback to every component node group found by nodeGroupRanges and reassembles the SVG string.

nodes.name: boundaryElements
nodes.summary: Scans raw SVG markup for boundary element ranges, mirroring nodeGroupRanges for boundary shapes.

nodes.name: transformBoundaryElements
nodes.summary: Applies a transform callback to every boundary element found by boundaryElements and reassembles the SVG string.

nodes.name: annotateArchitectureSideSvg
nodes.summary: Annotates one side's rendered SVG with added/removed/changed state markers on its node and boundary elements based on the compare receipt.

nodes.name: elementById
nodes.summary: Locates a specific SVG element's markup by kind and ID within a larger SVG string.

nodes.name: forceElementState
nodes.summary: Overwrites the change-state data attribute/class markers on a single SVG element's markup with a forced state value.

nodes.name: forceBoundaryState
nodes.summary: Overwrites the change-state markers on a boundary element's markup identified by key, mirroring forceElementState for boundaries.

nodes.name: buildDeltaSvg
nodes.summary: Merges the base and head SVGs into a single side-by-side delta SVG, prefixing element IDs per side and forcing element/boundary states from the compare receipt.

nodes.name: architectureDeltaChangeRows
nodes.summary: Flattens the compare receipt's grouped changes into a single ordered list of change-navigator rows for the delta viewer UI.

nodes.name: expectedReviewTargetSignature
nodes.summary: Computes the expected set of primary review tags a change row's delta markup must exhibit, used to validate that every row keeps an exact, enabled review contract.

nodes.name: renderArchitectureDeltaHtml
nodes.summary: Assembles the complete standalone architecture-delta HTML document: merged delta SVG, change navigator, legend, and interactive review scripting, given the compare receipt and both sides' rendered artifacts.
nodes.languageNotes: The largest function in the module (~460 lines), generating a full self-contained HTML/CSS/JS document as a template string.

nodes.name: validateArchitectureDeltaHtml
nodes.summary: Validates a rendered architecture-delta HTML document against its compare receipt, checking that every change row keeps its expected review-target signature before the artifact can be committed.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Concorde is a specification-driven development framework for Codex and Claude: it turns a change request into a reviewed, validated candidate through explicit software contracts called Module Specs. The README explains the core promise -- every agent task gets a complete Spec, phase-specific file access, and a recorded context -- and previews the capabilities that make the workflow inspectable end to end. Keep this promise in mind: the rest of the tour shows exactly how 'contract in, verified candidate out' is implemented in code.

tour.title: The Root Module Spec
tour.description: Concorde documents itself using its own methodology: this root Module Spec states the Framework's purpose, eight requirements and eleven usage scenarios, then lists the six child Modules -- Spec, Harness, Development, Reflections, Distribution and Views -- that together realize every promise. Notice that this root Module binds no implementation files of its own; it exists purely as the composition of its children, proof that a Module is a unit of specification rather than a physical directory or package. This is your map for the rest of the tour: each numbered step below corresponds to one of these six submodules or the infrastructure around them.

tour.title: Spec Protocol: The Four-Part Contract
tour.description: Before touching code, it helps to understand the contract language every Module Spec is written in. The Spec Protocol principles define the four mandatory parts of any Module -- Purpose, Requirements, Scenarios and Ontology -- where Purpose/Requirements/Scenarios form the 'functional spec' (what the Module promises) and the Ontology (entities plus labeled relationships) forms the 'architecture spec' (how it is built). The module chapter adds the rules distinguishing structural composition from mere dependency, and how implementation files are bound to a Module as metadata without ever supplying a promise the Spec omits.
tour.languageLesson: Requirement language follows RFC-2119-style keywords: MUST/SHALL states a hard requirement, MUST NOT a prohibition, SHOULD a recommendation that may be departed from for a stated reason, and MAY an allowed choice. Every requirement is exactly one SHALL sentence, so it can always be judged true or false against the Module.

tour.title: Global Entry Point: capabilities/main.py
tour.description: With the contract vocabulary in hand, here is where a session actually begins. capabilities/main.py is Concorde's global entry capability: it answers questions, routes work, and designs or applies system topology, importing the Agent inventory and the coordinator and spec_author bindings directly. It is the highest-scoring entry-point candidate in the whole codebase -- broad fan-out, shallow file depth -- making it the natural first stop once you leave the documentation layer.
tour.languageLesson: Capability modules are thin Python entry scripts that validate a request shape and then hand off to the shared development host, keeping routing logic separate from execution logic.

tour.title: The Trusted Execution Engine
tour.description: Every capability, including main.py from Step 4, ultimately routes through capability_host.py. It is the single node with the most outgoing dependencies in the project (13 imports), reaching into configuration, distribution's build pipeline, four Harness modules and four Spec modules in one file. This is the Development Module's core: the deterministic host adapter that freezes context, dispatches to the right Agent, and enforces isolation for every invocation Concorde runs on itself.

tour.title: Agent Roles: Coordinator & Spec Author
tour.description: Following main.py's own imports one level out, you land on the Agent inventory: agents/__init__.py declares the canonical AGENTS tuple, while coordinator/__init__.py and spec_author/__init__.py define two of its members. The coordinator Agent answers questions and routes work from complete Spec contexts, while spec_author reconciles a target's complete Markdown Spec collection -- these are two of the eight named roles (alongside planner, task_author, implementation_worker, context_assessor, code_reviewer and spec_reviewer) that the harness launches for each phase of a change.
tour.languageLesson: Python package __init__.py files act as a registry/barrel: each Agent's own __init__.py defines the role, and the package-level __init__.py re-exports them into one canonical tuple that the host can iterate over without hardcoding names.

tour.title: The Harness: Binding, Permissions and Context
tour.description: Agent definitions from Step 6 are inert until the Harness binds them to an actual execution. agent_model.py resolves each named Agent's Spec and build state into a reproducible AgentBinding; permissions.py compiles that binding's declared effects into a least-privilege policy and renders it into concrete Codex/Claude native configuration; context.py builds the immutable Spec, discovery and topology snapshots an Agent is allowed to see. Together these three files implement Concorde's central architectural idea: an agent's behavior is governed by two things, context and permission, both anchored to the Spec.

tour.title: The Spec Repository and Registry
tour.description: The context that Step 7's context.py freezes has to come from somewhere -- that source is the Spec repository. repository.py loads the project's Module registry, parses Module documents and exposes them by stable ID, while typed_data.py is the single most depended-upon file in the codebase (21 incoming references): a versioned TypedValue envelope validated at every capability and leaf data boundary. This is the Spec Module: the ontology, requirements and scenarios you read about in Steps 2-3 are not just prose, they are loaded, parsed and validated by this code.

tour.title: Distribution: Build and Validate
tour.description: capability_host.py from Step 5 also imports build.py directly, because a Module's Spec alone is not what an agent runs -- it has to be rendered into deployable Agent and Skill projections first. build.py is a deterministic, network-free renderer that turns authored sources under agents/, prompts/ and skills/ into those projections, and package_validation.py is the single validator that checks the resulting agents/, capabilities/ and skills/ inventories for consistency. This is the Distribution Module: it keeps the installed integration honest against the authored Framework source.

tour.title: Reflections: Tracking Gaps
tour.description: Not every promise gets fulfilled on the first try. The Reflections Module retains, investigates and resolves explicitly attributed project feedback and gaps without deciding product behavior itself. reflections.py parses per-file project reflection documents (the bucket/path conventions you would see under .concorde/reflections), and scoped_triage.py coordinates triage and implementation from within a Module-scoped invocation -- closing the loop back to the Development and Spec Modules from Steps 5 and 8.

tour.title: Harness Module Spec
tour.description: Now pair the Harness code from Step 7 with its formal contract. This module.md is the Harness's own reading entry: its Purpose states freezing context, binding Agent definitions, compiling and enforcing permissions, and executing invocations in fresh native processes coordinated as LangGraph graphs. Its Ontology names the exact entities you just read in code -- Context resolution, Agent and Harness model, Permissions, Agent execution -- proving the four-part Spec structure from Step 3 is not just theory but the literal specification this submodule's code implements.

tour.title: Public Skill: concorde-dev-loop
tour.description: Everything from Steps 4-10 is internal machinery; this is how a developer actually triggers it. The concorde-dev-loop Skill is an installed Agent Skill projection -- generated by the Distribution build from Step 9 -- that a developer's own Claude or Codex workspace can invoke directly. Calling it routes one change through specification, Spec review, planning, tasking, implementation, validation and code review, driving the whole capability_host.py pipeline from Step 5 to a ready candidate.

tour.title: Project Registry State
tour.description: This is the actual data repository.py from Step 8 loads for this checkout. specs.json is Concorde's own explicit Module registry: it enumerates the same seven Modules (root plus the six children from Step 2) with their parent/uses relationships, registered document collections and bound implementation files, alongside the deterministic checks used to validate readiness per Module. config.json pins the Architecture Profile and the accepted Spec Protocol version with its manifest digest, tying the abstract Protocol from Step 3 to one concrete, versioned configuration.
tour.languageLesson: JSON registries like this pin explicit schema versions (here, registry schema v3) so that a runtime can refuse to silently reinterpret an older configuration -- migrations must be explicit rather than inferred from file shape.

tour.title: Continuous Integration: Validating the Framework
tour.description: As a capstone, this GitHub Actions workflow gates every pull request and push to main by exercising nearly everything you have toured: it builds and validates the Concorde package (Step 9's build.py and package_validation.py), runs the full Python test suite covering the Development, Harness, Spec and Reflections Modules, and checks the docsite for type errors and build currency, with a separate job for the optional Studio test suite. If this workflow passes, every contract you have seen in this tour -- Spec, Harness, Development, Distribution and Reflections -- is verified consistent together.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows are structured as `on` triggers (pull_request/push), `jobs` that can run in parallel, and `steps` executed sequentially within a job; this workflow uses a separate job for the optional Studio suite so a failure there does not block the required checks.
